messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: P99 latency spike on /v1/streaming in eu-west-1 — p99 increased from ~2.4s -> 6.2s, p95 from 420ms -> 1.1s. Error budget burn detected. alert_id=INC-3819802468 :rotating_light:

arjun (oncall): paging @devon and @lina. Noted streaming stalls and tail piling up. Oncall taking lead.

devon: on it. seeing correlated increase in fetch latency to prefix-cache (kvstore) — hit-rate dropped sharply. pulling logs.

lina: I saw a config rollout earlier this morning around 3819700000 — prefix-hash salt changed to "v2-salt-2026-03". Could be related.

maria: customer-impact: CS reported two enterprise customers seeing degraded streaming for chat widgets. Some sessions stuck in buffering for >5s. Support queued a mitigation.

emily (sre): quick metrics dump:
- total streams 12k -> request backlog growing
- streaming stalls %5 -> ~12%
- prefix cache hit-rate: 92% (baseline) -> 14% (last 10m)
- kvstore 95th latency: 6ms -> 120ms, 99th: 18ms -> 860ms
- origin model latency unaffected when bypassing cache

ops: attaching tail logs snippet:
```
[kvget] prefix=v2:abc123 key=/stream/xyz -> MISS (namespace-salt mismatch?)
[kvget] backend=redis-8a region=eu-west-1 latency=842ms
[stream] conn_id=0x7f2a stall=6.2s p99
```

arjun (oncall): Hypothesis: prefix-hash rollout introduced new salt causing cache namespace mismatch -> massive cold-miss storm -> backend thrash -> streaming tail. Plan: 1) pause/rollback rollout 2) enable temporary read-through to origin for misses 3) warm-up keys for heavy prefixes 4) notify affected customers.

devon: rolling back prefix-hash to previous salt now. command: `deploy-config rollback --name prefix-hash --to-tag v2026-03-08-stable` — starting rollback (ETA ~90s).

lina: I also recommend toggling `enable_kv_prefetch`=false to reduce extra load on kv pods while we stabilize. Doing that on a small canary now.

maria: Support escalation: sending proactive note to two customers (Acct-453, Acct-992). "We are aware of increased latency and are mitigating; you may see transient reconnects".

emily (sre): Watching the backend. If kv latency doesn't drop in 3 min, we open emergency scale for kv cluster and enable extra read capacity.

incident-bot: ACTION: Rollback job started by devon at 3819802580. watch_id=rbk-3819802580. Progress updates will be posted.

devon: rollback completed on control plane — config reverted at 3819802642. Cache namespace should start matching old keys; expecting warm hits to return gradually.

ops: immediate metrics after rollback (30s window):
- prefix cache hit-rate jumped 14% -> 48% (first pass)
- kvstore p99 dropped 860ms -> 220ms
- streaming p99 dropped 6.2s -> 3.0s

arjun (oncall): Good. Next: warmup plan — prime hot prefixes for top-50 keys from recent traffic. I'll run a warmup job that will reseed KV with common prefixes at low QPS.

lina: warmup job kicked off: `scripts/prefetch_top_prefixes --window=30m --limit=50 --concurrency=8` — job id warm-3819802700.

maria: Notifying customers update: short message sent, offering follow-up and status page link. Support will track any new incidents.

emily (sre): After warmup completes (expected +2m) we should see hit-rate >80% and p99 <1.2s. If not, escalate to scaling or rollback routing to fallback region.

ops: warmup logs (sample):
```
prefetch prefix=v2:hot_42 -> wrote 12 keys
prefetch prefix=v2:hot_17 -> wrote 8 keys
throttle qps=25
```

incident-bot: NOTE: Temporary mitigation applied: read-through enabled for misses for 10m to reduce client stalls. Config flag `kv_readthrough=true` set at 3819802720.

devon: Observability note: add a short-lived stream-level metric `prefetch_hit_before_stream` so we can correlate in next incident. Filing a small follow-up ticket.

arjun (oncall): Handoff checklist to next oncall (@emily):
- incident summary: prefix-hash rollout caused cache namespace mismatch -> cold miss storm -> kv latency + streaming tail
- actions taken: rollback prefix-hash (rbk-3819802580), disabled kv prefetch canary, started warmup (warm-3819802700), enabled read-through for 10m
- customer impact: two enterprise accounts reported buffering; support notified and sent proactive messages
- monitoring to watch: prefix cache hit-rate, kvstore p99, streaming p99, error budget burn rate
- follow-ups: small infra ticket to add preflight check for prefix-rollouts, runbook update to include warmup step, create postmortem if SLO breach confirmed

emily (sre): Taking over. I'll monitor for 30m and coordinate postmortem. Thanks team.

maria: Thanks. support-bot will continue to collect customer logs and escalations into ticket TKT-381980-INC.

incident-bot: Incident resolved-to-monitoring at 3819802765. Please file follow-up items in the runbook: - preflight checks; - automated warmup; - customer communication template.

arjun (oncall): Closing live bridge. Handing to emily for post-incident. Good recovery — keep an eye on rollout gating. :thumbsup:
